title: A Horizon for the Gravity Again
premise: Oscar Underhill has spent eleven years alone tending the Svalbard seed vault and its mysterious beacon, a signal he inherited from a predecessor who vanished. When the deep-space vessel Meridian returns with a crew biologically aged backward into childhood, Oscar becomes the unlikely mediator between the ship's regressed survivors and the orbital fleet that exiled them, discovering the beacon was built to call them home. As the fleet's fragile truce collapses, Oscar learns the vault's cryo-banks hold two half-populations — Earth's loyalists and the Meridian's families — with power enough to wake only one. In the end, Oscar sacrifices his own place in the waking order, splitting his rationed years between both halves so neither side wakes alone, and the children of the Meridian plant the first seeds on thawing ground.
about_author: Wendell Reyes is a former Arctic logistics coordinator who spent three winters resupplying remote research stations before turning to fiction. He writes quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who keep the lights on after history moves on.

chapters.title: The Man Who Winds the Beacon
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A day in the rhythm of solitary maintenance: diesel generators, frost-sealed corridors, the nightly rotation of the beacon array nobody answers. Through his logbook entries we learn of his predecessor's disappearance and Oscar's quiet grief for a world that forgot him. Emotional beat: devotion hollowed into habit.

chapters.title: A Light That Answers
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The beacon receives an acknowledgment ping — the first in decades — then a distress transmission in a child's voice using protocol codes only adults would know. Oscar breaks containment procedure to respond. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as he realizes the voice is real and impossibly young.

chapters.title: Meridian Descending
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The ship makes a brutal landing on the ice shelf near the vault. Oscar treks out through a whiteout and finds a functioning vessel crewed by thirty children in adult-sized uniforms, all wearing the faces of people listed dead twenty years ago. Emotional beat: awe and terror in equal measure.

chapters.title: Children in Grown Men's Coats
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Oscar and Vess, the eldest of the regressed crew at twelve years old but carrying fragmented adult memories. They negotiate trust over shared rations; Vess remembers Oscar's predecessor. Emotional beat: two lonely caretakers recognizing each other across impossible difference.

chapters.title: What the Fleet Left Out
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Fragmented memories surface: the Meridian was sent to seed distant worlds, declared lost, and its return was never sanctioned because what happened aboard implicates fleet command. Vess hides the worst memory from Oscar. Emotional beat: guilt as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Fleet POV through Commander Ilsa Reyes-Okonkwo (no relation to the author), who detects the Meridian's landing and convenes a council bound by a truce expiring in forty days. She orders a retrieval team, officially humanitarian, unofficially otherwise. Emotional beat: duty tightening like a noose.

chapters.title: Seeds and Silence
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He shows the children the vault — millions of seeds, and beneath it, cryo-banks holding ten thousand sleepers in two sealed wings. The children react to Wing A and Wing B differently; Vess goes pale at one nameplate. Emotional beat: the vault revealed as a vault of people, not plants.

chapters.title: The Retrieval Team Lands
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Oscar and Ilsa's team leader Dr. Anselm Kade. The fleet arrives with medical scanners and legal writs; the children scatter into the ice tunnels. Kade is decent, which makes him more dangerous. Emotional beat: kindness weaponized by bureaucracy.

chapters.title: Backward Is Not Innocent
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Under Kade's gentle questioning, fragments assemble: the crew aged backward deliberately, a desperate experiment to escape something they witnessed or did out beyond the heliopause. Vess chooses to lie to protect the others. Emotional beat: a child learning to carry an adult's secret.

chapters.title: Two Wings, One Power Grid
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The fleet engineers discover the cryo-banks draw from a single failing reactor: reviving either wing fully will drain the other past recovery. Command orders Wing A — fleet loyalists — prioritized. Oscar realizes he holds the manual override. Emotional beat: the weight of an unasked-for choice.

chapters.title: Forty Days, Thirty-Six Left
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Political pressure mounts as the truce deadline approaches; factions frame the children as evidence, assets, or abominations. Ilsa privately reviews the Meridian's black-box partials and sees her own sister's name in the crew manifest. Emotional beat: the personal breaking through the institutional.

chapters.title: The Predecessor's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Decoding his predecessor's final encrypted logs, Oscar learns the beacon was commissioned to guide the Meridian home — and that the regressed crew are the experiment's second generation, grown from the original crew's cells. His predecessor chose exile rather than report it. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Vess Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. A fever triggers total recall: the crew found something out there, tried to become new to survive it, and the 'something' is still following the Meridian's wake toward Earth. Vess confesses everything to Oscar. Emotional beat: relief and horror arriving together.

chapters.title: Kade's Report
chapters.summary: Kade's POV. Ordered to falsify findings declaring the children nonviable, Kade instead sends the truth encrypted to Ilsa and goes dark, sheltering in the vault tunnels. The fleet brands him a deserter. Emotional beat: conscience priced in career and safety.

chapters.title: The Choice Made for Him
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Fleet command seizes the override remotely and schedules Wing A's revival; the children will be held as material witnesses indefinitely. Oscar, betrayed by the system he served, plans sabotage with Kade and Vess. Emotional beat: loyalty inverted into resistance.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Long Dark
chapters.summary: Triple POV, intercutting Oscar, Vess, and Kade during the blackout operation. They sever the grid, forcing a physical standoff in the cryo-wing as fleet marines arrive. Vess is caught shielding the younger ones. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into ferocity.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Verdict
chapters.summary: Isla's POV. Confronting Oscar at gunpoint among the sleeping pods, Ilsa reads Kade's leaked black-box data confirming what follows the Meridian — and that a united, awake population is humanity's only defense. She countermands command. Emotional beat: duty redefined as protection, not obedience.

chapters.title: Half and Half
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. With hours before the approaching threat enters sensor range, Oscar executes his own solution: stagger the revival, waking half of each wing now, half later, stretching the reactor past every safety margin — including the banks' reserve allocated to himself. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely at last.

chapters.title: What Followed Them Home
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The thing from the deep arrives — vast, patient, drawn to the beacon — and the freshly woken, groggy half-populations must work alongside the regressed children to blind it, using the beacon itself as a lure turned trap. Emotional beat: strangers becoming a single crew under fire.

chapters.title: The Beacon's True Commission
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, fading. Oscar stays at the array to hold the lure pattern as the others evacuate, spending his reserved life-support allocation to keep the signal true. The entity turns away from Earth, following the false horizon out. Emotional beat: the caretaker's final winding, serene and unflinching.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Vess's POV, months later. The remaining sleepers wake in shifts; the reactor holds, barely. Vess, now aging forward again, leads the children and the revived colonists in planting the first spring sowing above the vault. Ilsa resigns her commission to stay. Emotional beat: grief braided with beginnings.

chapters.title: A Horizon for the Gravity Again
chapters.summary: Vess's POV, epilogue. At the repaired beacon, Vess leaves a message for whoever comes next — and for Oscar, wherever his signal ended up — logging the vault's new commission: not preservation, but return. The last line mirrors Oscar's first logbook entry. Emotional beat: belonging finally answered, the light kept burning by many hands.
